requirement:
Per-file annotation details in the coverage overview are collapsed
initially.
rationale: The requirement has one obligation: per-file annotation details in the coverage overview are collapsed in the initial rendering. `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[documented_items_are_counted_once_with_browsable_directory_and_file_groups]` is marked `{test}` for it. It renders files in the root, `src` and `src/deep`. For each, it takes the card from the `file_card` helper. The helper returns the file row plus its nested detail table, up to the closing ``. The test asserts that each card contains `aria-expanded="false"` on the toggle button and a `hidden>` marker. That means the toggle reports collapsed and the detail row is hidden at render time. The test also covers the different shapes of detail content: single and multiple annotations, with and without explanations. It asserts that the root-level file row is not itself hidden, so the details are what is collapsed. Directory groups are `open`, which is a separate requirement. `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_browses_all_proposals_while_cli_checks_reviews_and_measurements]` is also marked. It renders the "Documented coverage gaps" chapter in several states. Those states are missing review, reviews recorded as true, false and FIXME, and covered. In each state it asserts that the `data-file="code.rs"` details are present. It also runs `exercise_file_click`, which executes the emitted click handler in Node against the real button and detail-row IDs. That shows the initially collapsed details can be expanded. Together the tests assert both the collapsed attributes on the rendered output and the toggle behaviour. A renderer that emitted expanded details (`aria-expanded="true"`, or no `hidden`) would fail the `book.rs` assertions. I found no unaddressed gaps.

text: Per-file annotation details in the coverage overview are collapsed
